quotes.text: # Collect physical addresses and phone numbers
Learn how to collect addresses and phone numbers during one-time payment flows.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: Set the value to `'billing'` or `'shipping'` to choose which Address Element shows the checkbox. Set it to `'none'` to hide the checkbox, or leave it blank to use the default value (`'billing'`).

In a multi-page checkout flow, you can manually [update the PaymentIntent](https://docs.stripe.com/api/payment_intents/update.md) or [update the Customer object](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customers/update.md) with the address details received from the `change` event or `getValue` method before moving to the next step.

findings: The November 7 exact-URL capture contains the title, one-time-payment purpose, and two links to Checkout Sessions embedded-components and Payment Intents Elements variants (new raw lines 5-14). The older same-URL capture bundled both full variants (old raw lines 18-345 and 347-727). The diff reflects presentation/navigation extraction, not evidenced removal of Address Element capabilities or changed API behavior.

The current mapped source summarizes the two API paths and their different constructors and React components (source lines 13-25), Checkout sync checkbox and default (lines 29-40), Payment Intents getValue and multi-page handling (lines 52-65), autocomplete with own key and CSP (lines 79-90), and confirmation validation (lines 92-94). Those statements align with the dated old guide's corresponding sections. The Stripe index and stripe-address-element concept already route to this source.

Keep source raw_files pointing to the full April guide as its dated factual evidence. The November index can serve navigation to variants but should not be added as technical backing for the existing source. Neither linked variant body was captured in this assigned evidence unit.
substantive_changes: No substantive address collection, autocomplete, validation, or API-path behavior change is established by the new 14-line index; the observed change is navigation to two query-parameter variants.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Checkout Sessions uses checkout.createBillingAddressElement/createShippingAddressElement and separate React checkout components; Payment Intents uses elements.create('address', {mode}) and AddressElement (old raw lines 98-113,170-208,404-447,494-531).
Checkout syncAddressCheckbox applies when both address elements are used and defaults to billing; shipping and none are other choices (old raw lines 304-339).

In the old guide, automatic address handoff occurs on confirming the single-page Checkout Session or PaymentIntent/SetupIntent, while a multi-page Payment Intents flow can manually update the PaymentIntent or Customer from change/getValue (old raw lines 238,577-579). Confirmation is an attempt and is not proof of successful payment.
Stripe-provided autocomplete key is conditional on same-group Payment Element or active Link session; elsewhere a merchant Google Maps key and stated CSP directives apply (old raw lines 585-594).
unresolved_questions: The November index supplies URLs but not the content of its Checkout Sessions and Payment Intents variants, so current detailed syntax, eligibility, defaults, and validation behavior remain unverified by this capture.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/advanced/collect-addresses, the November capture is a variant index (new raw lines 9-14) linking Checkout Sessions embedded components and Payment Intents Elements. The prior same-URL guide includes both full branches (old raw lines 18-345 and 347-727). [[source-stripe-collect-addresses]] already maps these distinct paths, so this capture establishes a navigation change rather than a substantive change to address collection or payment behavior.
answers.Q2: The dated [[source-stripe-collect-addresses]] can retain its existing technical summary for https://docs.stripe.com/payments/advanced/collect-addresses: old raw lines 98-113 and 404-447 show different API constructors, old raw line 339 gives the Checkout sync-checkbox default, and old raw lines 577-579 distinguish automatic single-page handoff from manual multi-page updates. New raw lines 11-14 only route to the two variants and do not revalidate their present contents. No source correction is required on this evidence.
